allowSame.wheel.nLabel: Dutch math terminology borrows "modulus" unchanged from the same Latin root English uses, so "N — modulus" is genuinely identical in nl and en
allowSame.wheel.nRangeLabel: Dutch borrows "Modulus" unchanged (same Latin root), so "Modulus N" is genuinely identical in nl and en
allowSame.wheel.roleProduct: Dutch borrows "product" unchanged (same Latin root), so the bare noun is genuinely identical in nl and en
allowSame.wheel.roleSum: Norwegian Bokmål's own word for the addition result, "sum", is spelled identically to English "sum" (both from the same Latin root) — a genuine cognate, not a missed translation

allowLiteral.Equivalence classes: ref-heading is JS-owned: render() overwrites its textContent on every load before first paint (the IIFE's final 'syncTabs(); render();' call)
allowLiteral.../Cayley Table/cayley-table.html?mode=: updateCayleyXref() builds an href string (code), not displayed prose; the cross-link's visible text is the separate static xref element, already translated via wheel.xref
allowLiteral.&lang=: the lang= URL parameter name, appended as code to the same updateCayleyXref() href so the cross-link carries the current language, mirroring decorateLinks' own lang= parameter

allowRenderText.N — modulus: Dutch math terminology borrows "modulus" unchanged from the same Latin root English uses, so the rendered nl label is genuinely identical to the English one (same as the dictionary-level allowSame entry for wheel.nLabel above)
allowRenderText.Modulus N: Dutch borrows "Modulus" unchanged (same Latin root), so the rendered nl aria-label is genuinely identical to the English one (same as the dictionary-level allowSame entry for wheel.nRangeLabel above)
allowRenderText.sum: Norwegian Bokmål's own word for the addition result is spelled identically to English (same as the dictionary-level allowSame entry for wheel.roleSum above)
